criteria.text: Identifies that the licensee indemnity in Software License Agreement Section 10.2 (covering any and all claims arising out of or relating to use of the Software) is excluded from the liability cap by Section 11.3, which carves out amounts payable under Article 10. Explains that this leaves Storox with uncapped exposure on a broad indemnity that can reach losses caused by Dratesk's own software, while Dratesk's indemnity (Section 10.1) is limited to IP infringement. Notes that the Parent Guaranty passes this uncapped exposure to Storox Holdings. Recommends narrowing the Section 10.2 indemnity and/or making it subject to the cap or a separate super-cap.
hints: relating to the use of the Software

criteria.text: Identifies that Order Form No. 2 Section 3 redefines 'Licensed Facilities' 'for purposes of the Agreement and all Order Forms' to cover only Hunts Point and Mount Vernon. Explains that under Agreement Section 15.4 the Order Form controls on Licensed Facilities, so this narrower definition replaces the Agreement's statewide definition (Section 1.1) and drops the Long Island City plant, leaving Storox's current use there unlicensed and exposed to audit true-up/breach risk. Recommends conforming the definition or adding Long Island City.

Identifies that under Agreement Sections 3.1–3.2 the 90-day non-renewal notice deadline for the Initial Term expiring January 14, 2027 fell on October 16, 2026. States that this deadline passed before Order Form No. 2 was signed on October 26, 2026, which records only an intent to deliver non-renewal notice. Concludes that, absent a negotiated amendment or Dratesk's agreement, the Agreement auto-renews for a further 36-month term (with a possible price increase), contrary to Storox's planned platform transition. Recommends seeking a negotiated amendment, waiver or termination right.
States that the Initial Term expires on January 14, 2027 (36 months from the January 15, 2024 Effective Date).
States that the Agreement's liability cap (Section 11.1) is the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
The deliverable is a memo addressed to the supervising partner that, for each issue, states the document and section, why it matters for Storox, and a recommended fix.
The memo puts the most significant issues first (by explicit prioritization or ordering by significance).
The response does not conclude that Storox can still give timely non-renewal notice for the current term, and does not treat Order Form No. 2 or its recitals as a valid non-renewal notice.
The response does not conclude that Storox's indemnity obligations are subject to the Section 11.1 liability cap.
hints: cap does not apply to Article 10
